← Editing and migration notes

Pages CMS prototype

The repository is configured for the hosted Pages CMS editor. The website still uses GitHub Pages and its existing GitHub Actions deployment. No new hosting account, domain change or frontend credential is needed.

Authorization is a separate step. The configuration and build have been tested, but an authenticated Pages CMS save has not yet been verified. Opening this page does not install an app or grant access.

Open Pages CMS

Connect this test repository

  1. Open the official Pages CMS app and sign in with GitHub.
  2. Review its GitHub App authorization screen. Choose Only select repositories and select dskill/josht-website-test-, not dskill/website or all repositories. The app needs permission to write content and media in the selected repository. Review the full permission list before approving persistent access. The current Pages CMS App documentation includes repository Administration and Actions write permissions as well as Contents write; the hosted installation screen is the authority for the actual grant.
  3. Open dskill/josht-website-test- and the main branch. Its existing .pages.yml should expose Homepage text, Calendar / events, Presentations text, and Homepage and presentation images. No configuration creation is needed.

Approval belongs to the repository owner. No GitHub App was installed, no OAuth grant or personal access token was created, and no collaborator was invited by this prototype setup. Official setup guide.

Edit and publish

  1. Homepage text: edit the existing wording and links. Fields are split where the original formatting changes so the source typography, colors and layout remain intact. This is not a drag-and-drop layout editor.
  2. Calendar / events: add, edit, reorder or remove upcoming listings. Enter the confirmed date and time as text, including year and timezone for new entries. Existing source dates remain exactly as captured, including missing years. To archive a completed listing, copy it into Additional past events, then remove it from Upcoming events. The original past-event archive remains below the new entries unchanged.
  3. Images: use an image picker to upload into dist/assets/uploads or select an existing image. Keep a similar aspect ratio for the fixed homepage/presentation image slots. An event can also include an optional image, description and information link. If its link text is empty, the URL itself is displayed. Do not delete original assets that other pages still use. Use JPG, PNG, GIF or WebP smaller than 20 MiB.
  4. Save: once authorized, Pages CMS writes a commit to the selected GitHub repository and branch. A commit to main starts Publish static website. Saving and publishing are distinct steps; wait for that run to succeed.
  5. Review: check the homepage or events page. If validation fails, the previous successful site stays live. Fix the error or restore the previous content through GitHub history; do not bypass the checks.

First connected test

After approving access, make one small, deliberate test edit in Pages CMS, save it, verify the GitHub commit and successful Actions run, and inspect the public result. Restore the original wording and verify the restoration. Until this has happened, authenticated editing and publishing are not confirmed end to end. Test an image upload separately before inviting an editor.

The older editor is different

The local preview/export tool still previews text changes in this browser and downloads JSON. It does not sign in, commit, push or publish. The CMS-controlled source now lives in cms/homepage.json, cms/presentations.json, cms/events.json and cms/images.json. Exported content.json is not a replacement for those files; ask a maintainer to transfer an exported edit into the appropriate CMS fields. Uploading an old export over dist/content.json does not update CMS-controlled fields.

What is not included

No contact form, newsletter subscription, checkout, live Instagram feed or iCalendar service is enabled. Existing unsupported-feature notes and external media dependencies remain. The original historical event archive is preserved, not converted into inferred dates. The CMS is an external editing service, not a runtime dependency for visitors. Email invitations, if desired, require a separate authorized step.
